name: Congenital Tricuspid Stenosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Echocardiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Tricuspid Stenosis

criteria.description: Thickened tricuspid valve leaflets with restricted mobility on echocardiography
Elevated mean trans-tricuspid valve gradient >5 mmHg measured by Doppler echocardiography
Right atrial enlargement detected by imaging modalities
Presence of characteristic murmur and signs of right heart failure

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of thickened tricuspid valve leaflets with restricted mobility and elevated transvalvular gradient on echocardiography
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on echocardiographic findings supported by clinical presentation.

laboratory: Elevated liver enzymes due to hepatic congestion
Mildly elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) levels
imaging: Echocardiography showing thickened tricuspid valve leaflets with restricted motion
Chest X-ray showing right atrial enlargement and possible cardiomegaly
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; may be associated with congenital heart defect syndromes
other: Electrocardiogram showing right atrial enlargement and possible atrial arrhythmias

distinguishingFeatures: Apical displacement of tricuspid valve leaflets
More pronounced tricuspid regurgitation than stenosis

references: Moss and Adams' Heart Disease in Infants, Children, and Adolescents, 9th Edition
American Heart Association Guidelines for the Management of Congenital Heart Disease
